Sasha Reynolds: Heads-up — CI evals for the quantized Llama-v2 bring-up are nondeterministic. pass@k flips between runs (0.62 -> 0.57) on the same commit. Repro: run ./scripts/run_evals.sh --suite=wpqa --model=llama-q8 --n_samples=20

Maria Chen: Ugh. Could be sampling + dedup ordering. Are we seeding RNG in the harness?

Aj Patel: Also check how we dedupe. If tokenization differs because of quantization A/B we can get different canonical texts and that changes c (num unique correct), which changes pass@k math.

Sasha Reynolds: Repro commands I used:
```bash
export CI_SEED=982341
./harness eval --config=ci/workplace_qa.yaml --model=llama-q8 --samples 20 --seed $CI_SEED
```
CI prints a seed but runs without it produce diffs. Link to failing CI: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/job/433

ci-bot: CI started for commit abc123 (seed=982341) :robot_face:

Maria Chen: Quick skim: our sampling is random.sample(candidates, k) with no stable ordering after dedup, and dedup uses raw string equality. Need: normalization (unicode NFKC, trim, collapse spaces), stable ordering, then deterministic sampling based on run seed + prompt-hash.

Aj Patel: For pass@k estimator, when we have all n distinct samples we can use closed form:
```python
# closed form pass@k when c successes among n
pass_at_k = 1 - comb(n-c, k) / comb(n, k)
```
But when we dedupe/collapse we must be careful to compute c on normalized outputs.

Sasha Reynolds: Good point. Also some of our tests mix exact match and BERTScore checks. For decode tasks we used exact-match, for free-form answers we use BERTScore >= 0.85. That config needs to be explicit in metrics.yaml per-suite. Right now the default is fuzzy and causes CI expectation drift.

Maria Chen: Proposed fix (will open PR):
1) canonical_normalize(text) using Unicode NFKC + strip + single-space collapse + lower() when config says so.
2) dedupe on normalized string.
3) stable list order: sort by (len(normalized), normalized) to keep order deterministic before sampling.
4) deterministic sampling: seed = global_seed ^ prompt_hash; use numpy.default_rng(seed).permutation(len(candidates))[:k] and then sorted indices so we preserve deterministic subset semantics.

Code sketch:
```python
def sample_k(candidates, k, seed, normalize_fn):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for c in candidates:
        n = normalize_fn(c)
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        uniq.append((n, c))
    uniq.sort(key=lambda nc: (len(nc[0]), nc[0]))
    if k >= len(uniq):
        return [c for n,c in uniq]
    idx = rng.permutation(len(uniq))[:k]
    idx = sorted(idx)  # stable ordering for downstream comparators
    return [uniq[i][1] for i in idx]
```

Aj Patel: Also add a test to CI: run eval twice with same CI_SEED and assert metrics identical (within floating eps for BERTScore). That will catch nondeterminism fast.

Sasha Reynolds: Edge-case: exact-match tasks should compute EM on normalized answers. BERTScore tasks should use the original text for embeddings but apply normalization to remove trailing punctuation differences if configured. Put thresholds in metrics.yaml per-suite so we don't mix rules.

eval-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/4330 — adds normalization + deterministic sampling + seed-assert test. CI triggered.

Maria Chen: I'll own the PR reviews and add tests for unicode edgecases (e.g. curly quotes, em dash).

Aj Patel: I'll change the pass@k metric impl to prefer closed-form when the candidate set is deterministic (n fixed), and fall back to empirical when we're sampling from an unbounded generator. Will add comments.

Sasha Reynolds: Nice. Also can we add a short doc in docs/evals/metrics.md explaining why dedupe+seed matter and how pass@k corresponds to both closed-form and empirical estimators? Saves future confusion.

Maria Chen: Yep, will add docs in the PR.

Sasha Reynolds: Thanks y'all. Leaving detailed followups on the PR. :thumbsup:
